name: Question 20
problem: Let $B={[\begin{aligned}17 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$  be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $S$ be the standard basis of ${R}^{2}.$ Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $S$ to $B.$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $S$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and ${{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}$, respectively. Recall that the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ consists of the vectors

$$
{e}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{e}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $S$ to $B$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $S$ relative to the basis $B.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${e}_{1}$ and ${e}_{2}$ relative to the basis $B.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {e}_{1} & {e}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}17 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{17}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{4}{17} & \frac{1}{17} & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{4}{17} & \frac{1}{17} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{17} & -\frac{4}{17} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=17{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{4}{17} & \frac{1}{17} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-\frac{4}{17}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

On the right-hand side, we obtain the change-of-coordinates matrix from $S$ to $B.$ Therefore, we have

$$
{P}_{S\to B}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -4 & 17\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 20
?

Let B={[174],[41]} be a basis of R2 and let S be the standard basis of R2. Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from S to B.

a
[1−4−44]
b
[1−4−417]
c
[12217]
d
[2−4−416]
e
[144117]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's denote the vectors of B and S as {b1,b2} and {e1,e2}, respectively. Recall that the standard basis of R2 consists of the vectors e1=[10],e2=[01].

The change-of-coordinates matrix from S to B is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors of S relative to the basis B.

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of e1 and e2 relative to the basis B. We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix M=[||||b1b2e1e2||||].

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

M=[174104101]R1:=117R1∼[141711704101]R2:=R2+(−4)R1∼[141711700117−4171]R2:=17R2∼[1417117001−417]R1:=R1+(−417)R2∼[101−401−417]

On the right-hand side, we obtain the change-of-coordinates matrix from S to B. Therefore, we have PS→B=[1−4−417].
